text: 9. The name here combines a root associated with curling high forms and another with a halo-bearing veil rather than a textured body. It is often so thin and elevated that its drama lies not in itself, but in what it does to the sun or moon — turning them into symbolic objects fit for prophecy, omen, or chapter endings. What is it?

10. This answer is one of the more aesthetically deceptive members of the family. Its name suggests a low heap, but in reality it often appears not as cheerful puffiness but as broad, lumpy fields, especially in cool, gray conditions. It is the sky equivalent of a blanket that cannot decide whether it wants to be soft or oppressive. What is it?
